title: Security says SQL is exposed
scenario: "Our scanner shows the SQL server accepting public connections. Close it — and make sure it cannot happen again." — Security operations (GD-06)
mission: Close public access through code and decide how to move the SQL guardrail from Audit to Deny without breaking the identity grant workflow.

prerequisites.notes: Sealed injection: sql_temporary_public_access=true applied by someone else.

steps.title: Find it
steps.command: az policy state list --filter "policyDefinitionReferenceId eq 'sqlNoPublicNetwork'" -o table

steps.title: Decide
steps.detail: Write the trade-off: Deny would block the grant script's firewall rule — what is the alternative path (jump pod in the VNet)?

criteria.text: SQL public network access is Disabled
An ADR or post-mortem records the Audit→Deny decision

expectedResult: Exposure closed and a decision on prevention.

concepts.title: Compliance is asynchronous
concepts.body: Policy compliance is evaluated after changes and periodically; results can take up to ~30 minutes. `az policy state trigger-scan` asks for an evaluation now.

concepts.title: Audit, Deny and the operational path
concepts.body: `Deny` prevents the bad configuration at request time. Before switching, check every legitimate process that needs the "bad" state — here, scripts that need temporary public SQL access — and give them another path (for example a job running inside the VNet).

concepts.title: Exemptions
concepts.body: An exemption excludes a resource from a policy for a reason and, ideally, an expiry date. It is for justified exceptions, not for silencing alerts.

example.title: listing non-compliant resources of one policy
example.body: Filter the policy states by the reference id inside the initiative:
example.code: az policy state list --filter "complianceState eq 'NonCompliant'" --query "[].{resource:resourceId, policy:policyDefinitionReferenceId}" -o table

glossary.def: Compliant / NonCompliant result of a policy evaluation.
Documented exclusion from a policy assignment.

recovery: Compliance can take up to 30 minutes to refresh; trigger a scan: az policy state trigger-scan.
dont: Do not create an exemption to silence it
hints: Which script needs your IP on the SQL firewall?
A job inside the VNet removes the need for public access.

interview.question: Policy flagged a public database. How do you fix it and prevent recurrence without blocking the team?

debrief: Fix the drift with Terraform; prevent with Deny once the operational path no longer needs public access. Exemptions are for justified, time-boxed exceptions — not for silencing.
